It is an application of ordinary causal sufficiency, not new information theory, and it does not say the system governs itself. | Active |

(2024) A is closed, its refinement (A, B) is not and the full state refining that is closed again, while A⊕B, a coarsening of (A, B), is not closed either; closure fails to be monotone because refining a description changes the future it must predict as well as the evidence, so Blackwell dominance, which every deterministic refinement has over its coarsening, does not order closure | Two readers' drafts of one point, from A6, A7, A16 and A17 of the exchange of 2026-10-20. A6 §6 and A7's Proposition 3: "Increasing the information retained by a representation can destroy a desirable dynamical property", and "There is no general data-processing inequality ordering these quantities, because both the predicted variable and the conditioning information change." This claim joins them, and corrects A7's slogan "When More Information Reveals Less Autonomy": closure is not reversed by refinement, it is unordered by it. Checked exactly on 2026-10-21. | Active |
